title: Plan Premium and Invoicing Terms — Real Estate Service Contracts
content:
These are the terms on which the plan premium of a Real Estate Service Contracts plan is set and invoiced.

**Clause A (retired) — no longer in force:** "The plan premium covers the whole buyer term and is invoiced once per order, payable through escrow at closing." This clause is superseded by the current basis: the plan premium covers the whole buyer term and is invoiced once per order, a plan change before closing crediting that invoice and reissuing it; on a buyer-only order before closing the buyer may pay part of it directly by card up to the direct card limit, and only on such an order, while the rest of the premium on such an order and the whole premium on every other order remain payable through escrow at closing.

**Clause B — premium amount.** The plan premium equals the plan's base premium, plus the oversize surcharge when the square footage is at or above the oversize threshold, plus the additional dwelling unit premium for each dwelling unit beyond the first, minus the condominium or townhome deduction when the property type is condominium or townhome. *This clause is no longer in force for a plan invoice reissued after a plan change before closing, whose invoiced amount is set by the current reissued plan invoice basis, and only for such an invoice; every other plan invoice still equals the amount this clause states.*

**Clause C.** Seller listing coverage carries no separate premium.

**Clause D (retired) — no longer in force:** "When the plan is changed before closing, the earlier invoice is credited in full and a new invoice is issued at the new plan's premium." This clause is superseded by the current basis: when the plan is changed before closing, the earlier invoice is credited in full and the reissued plan invoice is issued at the reissued plan premium of the current basis.

**Clause E (retired for reissued invoices) — no longer in force for a reissued invoice:** "The invoice is due on the closing date." It is superseded by the current basis: a plan invoice reissued after a plan change before closing is due on the expected closing date shown on the order, and only such an invoice; every other plan invoice remains due on the closing date.

**Clause F — when a premium may be invoiced.** The plan premium is invoiced only on an order in status listing coverage or awaiting closing. The status is read from the system record of the contract being invoiced, before the invoice is issued.

## Clause B in words, by part

| Part | Applies when | Effect on the premium |
|---|---|---|
| Base premium of the plan | always | the starting amount |
| Oversize surcharge | living area at or above the oversize threshold | added |
| Additional dwelling unit premium | for each dwelling unit beyond the first | added once per such unit |
| Condominium or townhome deduction | property type is condominium or townhome | deducted |

## Worked example under Clause B (hypothetical figures)

A hypothetical plan with a base premium of $500.00, an oversize surcharge of $100.00 at a threshold of 5000 sq ft, an additional dwelling unit premium of $300.00 and a condominium or townhome deduction of $50.00:
- a two-unit property of 5200 sq ft: $500.00, plus $100.00, plus $300.00 for the one unit beyond the first, giving $900.00;
- a one-unit condominium of 1400 sq ft: $500.00 less $50.00, giving $450.00.

## Clause F at a glance

| Contract status | Under Clause F |
|---|---|
| Listing coverage | invoicing permitted |
| Awaiting closing | invoicing permitted |
| Any other status | the plan premium is not invoiced |
